subject: Scope & next steps — GLBA / FERPA addenda and subprocessors

Subject: Re: Scope & next steps — GLBA / FERPA addenda and subprocessors

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Per our call, I wanted to get a concise scoping email over so your legal and procurement teams can confirm requirements.

Quick recap of asks from your side:
- GLBA addendum (data protection language for financial institutions)
- Clarification whether FERPA protections are required for any pilot datasets (we asked whether student-related PII might be present)
- Subprocessor list and any restrictions on outbound transfers (particularly to third-party cloud providers or to consultants outside the US)

What we can provide immediately:
- A current list of subprocessors (attached: redwood_subprocessors_20260301.csv)
- Draft DPA variant that includes GLBA-specific clauses we propose (attached: dpa-glba-draft.pdf)
- A short questionnaire template to accelerate technical scoping (attached)

Potential constraints we should flag now:
- For workloads that contain student records (FERPA), we typically recommend Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) or strict contractual controls; the hosted API can be used if only pseudonymized summaries are sent.
- For GLBA-controlled data where outbound transfer restrictions apply, we can offer Dedicated or Private deployments and additional contractual restrictions on subprocessors and cross-border transfers.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you can send the GLBA template your procurement team prefers (or comments on our draft), we’ll run legal and security review.
2) James Park from your consulting panel was mentioned as well — feel free to loop him in for compliance scoping.
3) If there are urgent data-residency requirements, let us know (we can engage our Private deployment team for timelines).

Would you like us to schedule a short 30-minute call with Marcus (legal ops) and Laura (security) to walk through the draft next Tuesday?

Thanks,

— Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0199

Subject: Re: Scope & next steps — GLBA / FERPA addenda and subprocessors

Hi Monica,

Thanks — helpful summary. Quick answers from our side:
- GLBA: yes, our counsel will need to include GLBA-specific contractual protections. We typically start from our in-house GLBA template and then negotiate carve-outs. I’ll attach our template by EOD.
- FERPA: pilot datasets are primarily account transaction and membership metadata; no student records are included for the initial pilot. That said, we have a separate product line that touches educational accounts and would need FERPA controls if we expand later.
- Subprocessors: we need the full legal names and locations of subprocessors (not just product names) and confirmation of whether any subprocessors are outside the U.S.

Two operational asks:
1) Can Redwood commit to keeping GLBA-controlled data within US data centers only for the pilot?
2) If we require a more restrictive subprocessor list, what is your typical turnaround to remove or restrict a subprocessor for a specific customer? (internal SLAs)

I’ve attached our GLBA template: GLBA_Template_GRCU_v1.docx

Would appreciate the short call. Tuesday morning ET works for me.

Best,

Sarah Lewis
Director, Vendor Risk & Compliance
GreenRiver Credit Union
sarah.lewis@greenrivercu.org

Monica — quick internal notes for the call and to prepare legal ops:

Summary of posture:
- Certifications: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and regular penetration testing; we can surface the current reports through an NDA.
- HIPAA/BAA: we already support BAA for healthcare customers; that playbook helps with contractual language and technical controls (audit logs, KMS key control, data-at-rest encryption keys per customer when on Dedicated/Private).
- GLBA: not a standard addendum we ship, but our legal team can negotiate GLBA-specific clauses using our DPA as a baseline. Key negotiation points will be cross-border transfers, subprocessors, and indemnity/notice timelines.
- FERPA: mostly an operational question — if there is any FERPA-controlled data, recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys; hosted API increases risk surface because of shared systems.

Answers to Sarah’s operational asks:
1) US-only residency: we can commit to US data centers for the pilot if they sign the Dedicated or Private deployment addendum; for hosted we cannot guarantee strict US-only residency unless explicitly configured.
2) Subprocessor restriction SLA: our typical timeline to enact a restriction (contractual suppression of a subprocess) is 4–6 weeks depending on partner agreements; removal may not be immediate if the subprocessor is critical for runtime (we can propose mitigation like IP whitelisting, limited access roles, or isolating the customer to a Dedicated pool).

Prep for the call:
- Laura, please prepare a short checklist of technical mitigations (VPC peering, dedicated keys, audit retention increase) and a one-page summary of what we can provide quickly vs. what requires product lead time.
- Rachel, please pull our latest subprocessors table with country of operations (I think the CSV Monica sent is the right one but double-check legal names and locations).

Will join Tuesday ET.

— Marcus
